name: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS)
summary_simple: A common hormonal and metabolic condition characterized by irregular ovulation, elevated levels of androgen hormones, and/or enlarged ovaries with multiple small follicles. It is a spectrum condition that affects how the ovaries function.

criteria.name: Ovulatory Dysfunction
criteria.description: Irregular periods (oligomenorrhea), absent periods (amenorrhea), or cycles lasting longer than 35 days or shorter than 21 days.

criteria.name: Hyperandrogenism (Clinical or Biochemical)
criteria.description: Signs of elevated male hormones (androgens), including excess facial or body hair (hirsutism), persistent cystic acne, or male-pattern hair thinning.

criteria.name: Polycystic Ovarian Morphology
criteria.description: Presence of 20 or more follicles per ovary and/or ovarian volume > 10ml, observed via pelvic ultrasound by a qualified sonographer/radiologist.
criteria.clinician_note: Requires a transvaginal or transabdominal ultrasound performed by a medical professional; cannot be diagnosed by self-assessment.

when_to_see_doctor: If you go more than 3 months without a period, have bleeding more frequent than every 21 days, notice sudden excess hair growth or hair loss, or struggle to conceive after 6 to 12 months.
sources: International Evidence-Based Guideline for the Assessment and Management of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (2023 / ESHRE / ASRM)
Rotterdam ESHRE/ASRM-Sponsored PCOS Consensus Workshop Group (2004)
American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) Practice Bulletin No. 194

name: Thyroid Dysfunction (Hypothyroidism / Hyperthyroidism)
summary_simple: Underactive or overactive thyroid gland regulating metabolism. An underactive thyroid often slows bodily processes, mimics PCOS cycle irregularities, and causes fatigue, weight gain, and cold sensitivity.

criteria.name: Biochemical Thyroid Hormone Abnormality
criteria.description: Altered serum Thyroid Stimulating Hormone (TSH) and Free Thyroxine (FT4/FT3) levels confirmed via venipuncture blood testing.
criteria.clinician_note: A primary differential that must be excluded before confirming a PCOS diagnosis.

when_to_see_doctor: If you experience extreme persistent fatigue, unexplained weight changes despite normal diet, heavy or irregular periods, or noticeable intolerance to cold or heat.
sources: American Thyroid Association (ATA) Guidelines for Thyroid Disease Management
Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guidelines on Hypothyroidism

name: Hyperprolactinemia
summary_simple: An elevated level of the hormone prolactin in the blood. Prolactin normally stimulates breast milk production, but excess levels can suppress ovulation, causing periods to become infrequent or stop entirely.

criteria.name: Elevated Serum Prolactin
criteria.description: High prolactin levels detected via laboratory blood test, which may be caused by benign pituitary microadenomas, medications, or thyroid conditions.
criteria.clinician_note: Essential differential to rule out in any evaluation for amenorrhea or oligomenorrhea.

when_to_see_doctor: If you notice milky breast discharge outside of lactation, persistent new headaches, peripheral vision changes, or missed cycles.
sources: Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline on Diagnosis and Treatment of Hyperprolactinemia
ACOG Committee Opinion on Amenorrhea Evaluation

name: Endometriosis / Pelvic Pathology
summary_simple: A condition where tissue similar to the lining of the uterus grows outside the uterus, causing inflammation, significant cyclic or chronic pelvic pain, and sometimes heavy menstrual bleeding.

criteria.name: Chronic Pelvic Pain & Dysmenorrhea
criteria.description: Severe pelvic pain often worsening around menstruation, during bowel movements, or with intercourse.

when_to_see_doctor: If menstrual pain is debilitating, prevents normal daily activities, or is accompanied by unusually heavy bleeding and pelvic cramps.
sources: World Health Organization (WHO) Factsheet on Endometriosis
ESHRE Guideline for the Management of Endometriosis (2022)
